open_decisions.question: Does Joe adopt the proposed subagent policy? CLAUDE.md currently says no parallel agents, apart from one read-only reviewer pass per mission, and BLUEPRINT section 9 says no fan-out.
open_decisions.proposed_default: Adopt a narrow policy at M2.gate.policy, with Joe editing the CLAUDE.md line himself. Read-only subagents may run at any time except during timed runs. At most one worktree writer runs at a time, in a sibling folder outside the repository that Joe adds with /add-dir in each session (never by editing .claude/settings.json, a judge file), on files no in-flight node writes, and runs only its own unit test. A lane never commits or merges: main copies its named files and runs check.py. No subagent starts hython, writes STATE, FACTS or README, or runs during timing. Joe edits BLUEPRINT section 9 or records that it may differ until the release. If Joe declines, the graph is the same: worktree and subagent nodes run on main in the listed order, and only the reviewer passes stay subagents.

open_decisions.question: Does M2 run attended or through tools/unattended.sh M2?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Attended, with the plan pause. Unattended takes three sessions, so only if Joe first writes a three-session budget into STATE, commits his answers to OD-03 to OD-09, accepts decision 0004, and a dry run shows an edit inside .claude/worktrees/m2 succeeds with nobody to approve it. In that case the reviewer pass and the env-prefixed values run happen in his attended session, and he merges only after 'No judge file touched' and a passing check.py.

open_decisions.question: How do analysis scale (required in the receipt), gain, gamma, luminance weights and fps reach the worker: a sidecar file or new flow flags?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Use a sidecar: <prefix>.json beside the analysis frames, with its own schema id cvcops.analysis_sidecar.v1 defined in decision 0004 and ARCHITECTURE. This needs no flow option and no change to controls.json, test_controls.py or the manifest argv. With no sidecar, scale is 1.0, defined as 'the analysis image is the source as given', and the rest are null. The sidecar is not in the cache key: weights, gain, gamma and scale change the analysis image and so its digest; fps alone does not. color_space stays null in v0.1. The alternative flag, --analysis-scale, would force maps_to.cli and collide with the string choices.

open_decisions.question: Which failures write an error receipt, and what do --backend opencl and cuda do in v0.1?
open_decisions.proposed_default: A preflight failure writes nothing: a missing or unreadable input, a bad argument or a refused backend. cuda with no CUDA device, and opencl with no usable device, exit 3. opencl with a device present exits 1, naming Mission 6. cpu runs call setUseOpenCL(False). A failure after both frames are hashed and read writes status error, removes that pair's old flow file and exits 1. The judge's backend test follows this rule, because the schema's backend.ran cannot be null.

open_decisions.question: What are verify's request flags and its JSON shape?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Optional --recipe, --backend and --tolerance (None means use the receipt's own values). --json prints {frames, counts {fresh, stale, missing}, pairs [{a, b, state, reason}]}. Exit 0 when all pairs are fresh, 1 otherwise, 3 for a broken environment. The manifest's verify argv carries the flags, and Check Cache passes the node's values, showing missing as an error and stale as a warning.

open_decisions.question: How are the build identity, the cache-key params, the pair statistics and the receipt paths defined?
open_decisions.proposed_default: build_sha256 is the SHA-256 of cv2.getBuildInformation() with line endings normalised. params.values holds tolerance_px, mask false, and the LF-normalised source hashes of read_analysis_exr, estimate_flow and validity. The engine version is not in the key. clipped_share and grey_levels take the worse of A and B. Paths are absolute POSIX.

open_decisions.question: What are the timings_s keys, what is flow compute, and how is the bake total measured for DEC.quarter?
open_decisions.proposed_default: The keys are read, hash, flow (forward DIS), validity (backward DIS plus the check), write and total, matching the locked example plus hash. flow_compute = flow + validity. worker_io = read + hash + write. total is the measured wall time of each run, from export start to the last load cook. The ratio is median flow_compute over median total across five runs, each with a fresh hython and an empty cache folder, no warm-up discarded, and no other python or hython process running.

open_decisions.question: Does jsonschema become a runtime dependency, and where do the new shapes and the bake receipt live?
open_decisions.proposed_default: jsonschema stays dev-only: the worker checks shapes by hand, and the tests validate against the locked schema. No new files under docs/contracts before v0.1. The sidecar (cvcops.analysis_sidecar.v1), verify JSON and cvcops.bake.v1 shapes live in decision 0004 and ARCHITECTURE, held by unit tests. The bake receipt goes in docs/facts/m3_bake_receipt.json (unlocked), and each bake writes a record at $cache/bake.json.

open_decisions.question: On which stream does flow report per-pair progress, and how does the glue read it without stalling?
open_decisions.proposed_default: One line per pair on stdout, printed with flush=True, with reasons on stderr. The glue starts the worker with -u as well, reads stdout line by line, and sends stderr to a temporary file whose last lines it keeps, so neither pipe can fill and block the other.

open_decisions.question: Which channel layouts must read_analysis_exr accept before M3 knows what ROP Image writes?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Widen the reader in M2. It accepts any single channel, or a bit-equal R, G, B trio with or without one layer prefix; it ignores alpha; it accepts FLOAT or HALF; and it crops a data window that contains the display window. M3 pins the real export as a fixture rendered directly, never cropped. If the reader refuses it, the prep writes R = G = B, or the network wires Mono into an RGB input implicitly; never the monotorgb node, which remaps through a ramp and clamps.

open_decisions.question: On Windows, does os.replace fail while a cooked File COP holds flow.####.exr open?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Assume it can fail. The writer retries for about a second, then fails the pair, writing an error receipt naming the lock when every field is measured. Bake reloads the File COP only after the worker exits. M3's bake smoke re-bakes with the scene loaded and records the result in FACTS.

open_decisions.question: Does a script-built OpenCL COP kernel cook under hython on 22.0.492?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Yes, proved by the probe's first line. If not, prep falls back to the stock Mono COP at HDTV Luminance, and Joe decides what Luminance Weights does. Convert has no one-node fallback, so stop and ask before building any chain.

open_decisions.question: Is the analysis image exported as RGB or Mono, how does the export keep the temp-then-replace rule, and must a re-export give identical bytes?
open_decisions.proposed_default: RGB, with the prep kernel writing grey into R, G and B (the P3-tested path); Mono only if the probe shows a name the reader accepts and a faster export. ROP Image writes into <cache>/.export/, and the Bake function moves each frame into place with os.replace. Export Properties and any other header metadata are off, and a re-export of unchanged pixels must give identical bytes, because the next pair's input digest depends on it in chunked bakes and partial re-bakes. If the probe shows it cannot, stop and ask; the proposed remedy is that Bake keeps an existing analysis frame that a fresh receipt references.

open_decisions.question: How do the three Status controls show text, given that label parms store no values?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Use a label whose column label is a backtick expression reading node user data that Check Cache sets. If the probe shows it never refreshes, ask Joe whether the three controls may become read-only string parms. That would change controls.json and tests/unit/test_controls.py, which are not judge files.

open_decisions.question: Is houdini/otls/ git-ignored, so that each user builds the asset?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Yes. Ship build_hdas.py and have tools/install.py build the asset under each user's own licence. No .hda goes into git or the GitHub release (P7: an Indie build is limited commercial).

open_decisions.question: What are the example scene's size, its outputs, and whether it is saved and committed?
open_decisions.proposed_default: 1920x1080 frames 1001-1025 (24 pairs), dis_medium, cpu, Analysis Scale 1.0, RGB export. Commit the scripts only; frames, renders and the saved scene go in examples/two_region/out/, which is git-ignored. Save only after Joe's go-ahead at the M3 plan pause. Time run 1 first, and if it exceeds 300 s, ask to shrink the example.

open_decisions.question: Can M3 close in one session?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Plan for two sessions, with the reason written in STATE first. The harness proves several parts per hython call.

open_decisions.question: How are the asset's HOM unknowns handled: typed ports through createDigitalAsset, how bake_once drives the bake, how the button reaches it, and loading from otls?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Carry the subnet port multiparms as hidden parms derived from controls.json. The PythonModule's callbacks import cvcops_houdini.bake inside each function, so the asset builds and self-tests before bake.py exists; bake_smoke proves the button resolves to cvcops_houdini.bake.bake, and bake_once calls that function directly. Loading the asset from <hpath>/otls at hython start without installFile is a hard pass in the self-test. If it fails, write BLOCKED: and stop: the cure is a package change in both src/cvcops/package.py and the locked impls.hython_env, so Joe re-locks. No installFile fallback, which would keep the judge green while artists get no asset.

open_decisions.question: How are licence losses and rung-1 timeouts classified?
open_decisions.proposed_default: A rung-2 FAIL whose message is a licence or hython start-up error counts as exit 3: write the blocked line and make no code edit. Never run two hython at once, and no hython while Joe's GUI is open. If pytest --durations pins a rung-1 timeout on a test this session added, trim that test and note it in STATE. Any other exit 3 is blocked.

open_decisions.question: Which Distort step mode pulls like cv2.remap, and if none passes 1.5 levels, is Flow Warp built?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Pixels per Step off (one lookup at p + f), confirmed on the suite and on a 150 px field. If no mode passes, stop and ask. The proposal is cvcops::flowwarp::1.0, built from a new hda_flowwarp names entry by the same builder and graded by the same row. Nothing is built before Joe says yes.

open_decisions.question: What fix does the M4 example carry, from which key frame, how far back, and with what look?
open_decisions.proposed_default: A soft-edged coloured mark painted on the disc at key frame 1024, carried back 8 frames (1016-1023) by an unrolled Distort chain and composited Over the plate. Joe can change any of these at the M4 start sitting.

open_decisions.question: If DEC.quarter says yes, do ME or M6 run before v0.1?

open_decisions.question: How is v0.1 distributed, and which new release files and branch does Joe allow?

The GitHub pre-release v0.1.0 carries install.py only, and that install.py clones the v0.1.0 tag, not main. The session commits a release/v0.1.0 candidate branch with Joe's consent. BLUEPRINT is not updated.

open_decisions.question: Where does install.py write the package file by default, and when does it rebuild the asset?
open_decisions.proposed_default: HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR with __HVER__ expanded if set, otherwise <Documents>/houdini22.0/packages from the Windows Documents known folder, because desktop Houdini reads that folder while hython and Git Bash's HOME point elsewhere (help:22.0.492/ref.zip/plugins.txt). Never HOME from the shell. --packages overrides, the path is printed, and Joe confirms it by eye; no hython run in his own environment. Rebuild when the asset is missing or its stamp file differs from the stamp of the current tree, plus a force flag; never by modification time.

open_decisions.question: What is Joe's plate, what may be committed, and how are defects it exposes handled?
open_decisions.proposed_default: An EXR sequence of at most 4K and 100 frames, kept outside the repository and baked in one call or in chunks under 600 s each. Only numbers are committed: no pixels, and no path beyond the spine's STATE record. Gain and gamma are his call. A defect is fixed in the release session if the fix stays inside the contract and the locked rows, with both rungs re-run; otherwise pause and ask.

open_decisions.question: Should the release prove a fresh clone, and should a .gitattributes pin line endings?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Yes to a fresh clone in the session scratch folder. No .gitattributes before v0.1; record what the CRLF checkout did, and rely on the LF-normalised lock and stamp.

open_decisions.question: Does Joe confirm labels before the M3 build, and does the tolerance default stay at 1.0?
open_decisions.proposed_default: Yes to both. Labels are confirmed at the plan pause from the table generated from controls.json, so the builder runs once. Changing contract.DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_PX is a contract change under flow-contract-v1.

open_decisions.question: What is the Frame Range default? With $FSTART to $FEND, Bake fails on any plate whose last frame is $FEND, because the export needs frame f2+1.
open_decisions.proposed_default: $FSTART to $FEND-1, so every baked frame has a successor in the scene's own range. The README's limits say so.

open_decisions.question: Does v0.1 go public without a licence file, and what happens to decision 0001's licence item?
open_decisions.proposed_default: v0.1 ships with no licence file and the README says so; default copyright applies. Decision 0001's licence item stays open, and only its release-gate box is ticked. Joe can choose a licence instead in the release plan pause.

cross_mission_contracts.contract: Every subagent and worktree node in M2, M3 and the release runs as a subagent or lane only if Joe adopted the policy at M2.gate.policy; otherwise it runs on main in the listed order. Lanes live outside the repository, never commit, and are copied back by main.

The Bake button calls $<env_prefix>_WORKER_PYTHON -I -u -m cvcops flow --in <cache>/analysis.####.exr --out <cache> --frames f1-f2 --recipe --backend --tolerance, with PYTHONPATH and PYTHONHOME also scrubbed by the caller. Exit codes are 0, 1 and 3 per decision 0004, with one flushed progress line per pair on stdout. Flow is stored at analysis resolution, never resized: R = u, G = v in opencv_px, B = valid.

verify takes optional --recipe, --backend and --tolerance, and --json prints {frames, counts {fresh, stale, missing}, pairs [{a, b, state, reason}]}. M2 fixes and documents this in ARCHITECTURE so M3 never reopens it.
Every receipt carries timings_s read, hash, flow, validity, write and total. flow_compute = flow + validity and worker_io = read + hash + write, so the M3 bake receipt and DEC need no M2 change.

The sidecar is <prefix>.json beside <prefix>.####.exr, schema cvcops.analysis_sidecar.v1 (its own id, not the receipt's), limited to analysis.luminance_weights, gain, gamma, scale, color_space and frame.fps. It is read by cvcops.receipt.read_analysis_sidecar; measured fields are refused; no file means scale 1.0, the source as given.

The reader accepts any single channel or a bit-equal R, G, B trio (with or without a prefix), alpha ignored, FLOAT or HALF, the data window cropped, rint(x * 255) clipped to 0-255. M3 adapts the asset (the prep writes R = G = B, or an implicit Mono-to-RGB wire; never the monotorgb node) rather than reopening the reader.
Worker temp names never match flow.####.exr or flow.####.json. os.replace retries for about a second and then fails the pair. The Bake function reloads the File COP only after the worker exits.
flow skips pairs that receipt.freshness calls fresh, and v0.1 has no force flag. Timed runs therefore use a fresh, empty cache folder, and the aggregator refuses any run with a skipped pair.
Receipts read engine.version from cvcops.__version__ at call time, and the engine version is not in the cache key. The 0.1.0 move reaches every new receipt without staling caches.

--backend opencl and cuda are refused in preflight with exit 3 (no runtime) or 1 (device present, no v0.1 recipe; names Mission 6) and write nothing. The README's CPU-only limit quotes this behaviour.

The hython path from local.toml, its size and sha256 are recorded at M3's start. M3.judge.close, M4's baseline and close, the fresh clone and the release close compare them, so a stand-in hython cannot pass rung 2.

docs/facts/m3_bake_receipt.json (cvcops.bake.v1) holds n = 5, raw runs, workload, medians_s {total, export, flow_compute, worker_io, worker_other, load, other} and quarter {ratio, at_least_a_quarter}. evidence/bake_receipt.py --check prints them. M6 and REL.release.numbers read the same file.
M3.judge.close writes the one 'DEC input' line into STATE before Joe's M3 commit. That line is DEC.quarter's proof; DEC.quarter adds only Joe's ME and M6 choice.

houdini/tests/bake_timing.py accepts --source, --frames, --out, --recipe, --backend, --colorspace, --gain, --gamma and --analysis-scale, as M3's plan named them. It drives bake(node) and is chunkable by frame range, so the release needs no new bake script.
With Export Properties off, re-exporting unchanged pixels gives identical bytes, so a chunk boundary or a partial re-bake leaves the neighbouring pair fresh.
cvcops_houdini.bake.bake(node) is the one bake callable, the same one the button runs. It writes $cache/bake.json last and returns the phase wall times. M4 and the release bake only through it.

The asset's Flow output is in Houdini image units (v up, half the longer side per unit), so Distort at Scale -1 pulls with no second conversion. The internal node names (source_in, prep, downscale, export, load, convert, out) are stable.

build_hdas.py takes --out DIR, names the file from [tool.cvcops.names], exits 0, 1 or 3, prints the licence category, and keeps houdini/otls/ git-ignored with no .hda committed. It writes houdini/otls/<file>.stamp.json from houdini/build/stamp.py, which hashes every build input with line endings normalised; install.py rebuilds when that stamp differs.

test_houdini_entry_points.py discovers every __main__ script under houdini/build, houdini/tests and houdini/examples, and requires exit 3 without hou within 10 s. M4's and the release's scripts are covered with no change to the test, as long as each keeps the hou check at the top of main().

evidence/package_install_check.py proves that package.py's own file, alone in HOUDINI_PACKAGE_DIR, loads the asset through hpath and sets the worker variable. The release re-runs it unchanged on the candidate.

examples/two_region/make_frames.py and houdini/examples/build_scene.py, with modes and example_network(parent, frames_dir) and frames 1001-1025 at 1920x1080. M4 adds the carry mode and the release adds the plate mode.
M3's passing rung 2 gives the mean wall time per hython bake call, projected onto M4's 19 calls under check.py's 3600 s, before M4 starts.

evidence/audit_receipts.py <cache> --frames <range> --expect-sidecar validates every receipt against the locked schema, checks the sidecar's schema id and recomputes freshness. The release audits Joe's plate with it unchanged.

pull_network(parent, b, flow, settings) in cvcops_houdini/pull.py, with the probe's step mode. M4 also reports to the release's README nodes whether native Distort passed or Flow Warp was built, and the step cap for large motions.
The DEC.quarter verdict line in STATE. v0.1 is CPU only unless Joe opened M6 and it adopted a recipe before release (default: not).
